gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a Galaxy Watch8 LTE can be worn by someone with no phone only through Samsung's 'Set up for a child' mode, which needs a one-time pairing from a parent's Samsung Galaxy phone (One UI 5.1 or later, Galaxy Wearable app, Family Link), and that on Verizon that phone must be on the same account as the watch; Samsung's own cited CA page instead says Galaxy Watch4 and later 'require a compatible phone during the initial setup'.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited pages, Apple 119601 (Set up cellular on Apple Watch) and Samsung CA (Set up your Galaxy Watch with or without a phone), and the uncited Apple 109036 (Set up Apple Watch for a family member). Apple 119601 already says the iPhone and watch must use the same carrier, and Apple 109036 already says a family member without an iPhone can use a cellular Apple Watch set up from a parent's iPhone. So the Apple half of 'who owns the phone' is covered. The Samsung CA page only says older Tizen models (Galaxy Watch, Active, Active2, Watch3) can be set up without a phone and that Wear OS models need one. It never mentions the Galaxy Watch for Kids path on Watch8/7/6 LTE or that it needs a Samsung phone. None of the results covers Pixel Watch: that the watch shares the phone's number, that it must be on the same carrier network as the phone, or that iPhones aren't supported.
decides: The page needs to split two cases. (1) The wearer owns a phone but wants to leave it at home: every big-brand LTE watch puts the phone's own number on a companion line. Apple and Google both require the watch and phone to be on the same carrier, so the shopper's phone carrier decides the pick. (2) The wearer has no phone at all, like a child or an older relative: only the Apple Watch SE 3 cellular (Family Setup from a guardian's iPhone), the Galaxy Watch8 LTE (Kids setup from a guardian's Samsung Galaxy phone, US only, Verizon/AT&T/T-Mobile at launch) and the TickTalk 6 work. The Pixel Watch 4 drops out of case 2 because I found no official path for it. Our current Galaxy Watch 8 cell, 'Samsung allows standalone setup on LTE models', is wrong as written. It should say: 'Only via Galaxy Watch for Kids, paired once from a parent's Samsung Galaxy phone; otherwise an Android phone is needed for setup.'

findings.label: Can be used without the wearer owning a phone
findings.value: Yes, via Galaxy Watch for Kids. Samsung's footnote 1 says 'Available on Galaxy Watch8 LTE, Galaxy Watch7 LTE and Galaxy Watch6 LTE'. The page says the watch works 'without needing their own phone'.
findings.source_title: Galaxy Watch: Now kid-ready | Samsung US
findings.note: From Samsung US maker page footnotes 1 and 2.

findings.label: What the guardian needs for kids setup
findings.value: Initial pairing with 'a compatible Samsung smartphone', a Samsung Account and a Google Account with Family Link, and a 'qualifying wireless plan with LTE service activated'. Verizon, AT&T and T-Mobile were named at launch. Samsung says carriers may not support standalone voice calling.
findings.source_title: Galaxy Watch: Now kid-ready | Samsung US
findings.note: The page doesn't say whether the child's watch gets its own phone number.

findings.label: Carrier rule for kids (standalone) setup
findings.value: Parent phone must run 'OneUI 5.1 or higher' with the Galaxy Wearable app. 'The companion smartphone must be activated on the same Verizon account as the Galaxy Watch8.'
findings.source_title: Samsung Galaxy Watch8 - Set Up in Standalone Mode (Kid Setup) | Verizon
findings.note: One UI is Samsung's Android skin, so in practice this means a Samsung Galaxy phone. Verizon sends adults who want setup without restrictions to Number Share ('Set Up for Myself').

findings.label: Google's own requirement list for Galaxy Watch for Kids
findings.value: 'A Samsung Galaxy phone and Galaxy Wearable app'. 'The Samsung Galaxy Watch for Kids is currently only available in the U.S.'
findings.source_title: Set up Galaxy Watch for Kids - Google For Families Help
findings.note: This page still names only the Galaxy Watch 7. Samsung's US page adds Watch8 LTE and Watch6 LTE.

findings.label: Normal (adult) setup
findings.value: Wear OS models '(such as Galaxy Watch4 and later) require a compatible phone during the initial setup'. Only older Tizen models (Galaxy Watch, Watch Active, Active2, Watch3) can be set up without a phone.
findings.source_title: Set up your Galaxy Watch with or without a phone | Samsung CA
findings.note: This is the cited rival page. It doesn't name Watch8, but Watch8 falls under 'Galaxy Watch4 and later'.

findings.label: How the LTE line works
findings.value: The watch 'Shares a number with your phone so notifications and messages are in sync'. You activate it from the phone's Pixel Watch app under Connectivity > Mobile network. 'Your Google Pixel Watch LTE doesn't need a phone to call emergency services' but it does need an active LTE connection.
findings.source_title: Google Pixel Watch 4G LTE features - Google Pixel Watch Help

findings.label: Carrier and phone requirement
findings.value: 'For full talk, text, and data functionality, Pixel Watch and Android companion devices must use the same carrier network.' 'iPhones aren't supported.' Pixel Watch 4 needs Android 11 or later.
findings.source_title: Google Pixel Watch Help - compatibility FAQ
findings.note: The same page lists a Pixel Watch 5 (Android 12 or later), so our Pixel Watch 4 row may be a generation behind.

findings.label: Carrier rule for normal pairing
findings.value: 'Your iPhone and Apple Watch must use the same carrier.' Watches set up with Apple Watch For Your Kids can use a different carrier, and international roaming isn't supported on them.
findings.source_title: Set up cellular on Apple Watch - Apple Support
findings.note: Already on a cited rival page. Included for comparison.

findings.label: Use by someone with no iPhone
findings.value: A family member 'who doesn't have their own iPhone can use their Apple Watch'. Requires a cellular Apple Watch Series 4 or later, or SE or later. A guardian's iPhone does the setup and management.
findings.source_title: Set up Apple Watch for a family member - Apple Support
findings.note: This page was in ChatGPT's results but not cited. As fetched, it gave old minimums (iPhone 6s / iOS 14 / watchOS 7), so I left those out of the value.

unsourced: An official Google statement on whether a Pixel Watch 4 or 5 LTE can be set up for a child or a phone-less wearer. I checked Pixel Watch Help 13541778 and 12652073 and searched Google Families Help, and found nothing either way.
Whether a Galaxy Watch8 LTE in kids setup gets its own phone number or shares the parent's. Samsung's kids page and Verizon KB 310633 don't say.
AT&T's and T-Mobile's own account rules for Galaxy Watch8 kids setup. The AT&T device-support URL I opened was a generic landing page.
